children.text: Elementary students engage in a comprehensive curriculum driven by project-based learning (PBL) and the scientific method in math, English, and science. They benefit from weekly sessions in swimming, physical education (PE), and gymnastics to support their physical development. The curriculum is enriched with music, art, drama, and French, in addition to Arabic plays and Qur’an recitation to strengthen cultural identity and creativity. Students are introduced to AI and STEM foundations, developing 21st-century skills at an early age.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi elementary teacher guiding students through a hands-on building activity

children.text: In Grades 1 and 2, SAIS - Abu Dhabi is implementing an ongoing assessment model designed to provide a comprehensive and holistic view of each student’s progress. This shift moves away from solely relying on periodic tests and instead focuses on continuous evaluation through observations, classwork, homework, projects, discussions, and quizzes. This approach enables teachers to better understand and support students’ development throughout the year in a relaxed and stress-free environment.

heading.title:
Assessment for Every
Stage of Learning

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi elementary student wearing safety goggles in a STEM workshop

children.text: While multiple formative and summative assessments will take place across subjects, parents will not be informed prior to their administration to ensure assessments reflect authentic learning and reduce performance anxiety. However, in response to parent feedback and to support home preparation, schedules will be shared in advance for Arabic and Islamic Studies assessments only.

We continue using our proficiency scale for Grades 1 and 2 to better reflect the progress and achievements of our students. We do convert these proficiency scales into percentages for our internal data analyses.

children.text: Our High School program focuses on university and career readiness. Students receive individualized support to pursue pathways aligned with their future goals. A wide selection of electives and advanced courses, including AP programs, ensures that students can explore specialized interests.

As an accredited College Board (AP and SAT) and IELTS testing center, we prepare students thoroughly for academic success beyond school. Daily schedules also include lab-based science, design and technology, computer-based learning, and volunteering opportunities, all aligned with graduation requirements and personal development.

children.text: The curriculum enables students to pursue a personalized pathway. Advanced Placement (AP) courses, elective options, and career guidance prepare students for university and beyond. children.text: High School Pathways function like college majors, but begin during the high school experience. Every student can benefit from selecting and following a sequence of career-related classes aligned with their interests.
A Pathway:
Provides a sequence of courses within your area of interest
Connects your career interests from high school to college and/or career
Serves as an educational roadmap guiding you to relevant high school courses and postsecondary options
Helps you acquire knowledge and skills linked to specific postsecondary programs leading to certificates, degrees, and careers

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi high school student painting a model in art class

cards.description:
Students in this pathway solve problems, develop new technologies, and drive innovation. This rigorous college preparatory curriculum focuses on advanced mathematics and science, preparing students for university-level work.

Participants apply essential math and science content in real-world contexts. Career possibilities range from science and math educators to laboratory technicians to NASA astronauts.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi high school students walking with their teacher in the girls section

cards.title: Science and Engineering Pathway

cards.description:
Students gain hands-on foundational skills in their chosen mode of expression, including:

•	Studio art
•	Fashion design
•	Interior design
•	Acting
•	Theater production
•	Vocal and instrumental performance
•	Film and audio production

This pathway develops cultural awareness alongside communication, creative, and critical thinking skills necessary for success across various fields. Graduates may seek direct employment as artists, musicians, designers, actors, or audio producers, or pursue bachelor’s or graduate degrees for careers in teaching, art direction, theater production, fashion, interior design, media arts, and film.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi teacher guiding two high school students sketching in art class

cards.title: Visual and Performing Arts Pathway

cards.description:
This pathway provides students with opportunities to develop skills for customer-focused careers and gain experience in technology, communication, and management. Students explore business ownership fundamentals and practice developing business plans while learning to organize and direct business operations.

Students investigate financial management, including how industry standards, economic factors, technological advancements, international influences, social trends, legal requirements, and ethical considerations impact business decisions. They learn to formulate and interpret financial information for decision-making, compliance, and risk management.

Career opportunities include entrepreneurship, sales, marketing, economics, management, accounting, banking, securities and investments, and other financial specializations.

children.text: Advanced Placement (AP) is a College Board program that allows high school students to take courses that can earn college credits and/or qualify them for advanced university classes. AP courses are weighted (1.25), provided students achieve qualifying scores on the respective College Board exams.
AP classes are optional. All enrolled students must sit for the College Board AP exam and cover the cost of required resources and exams.

children.text: Middle School students explore emerging interests while deepening their academic knowledge. In addition to core subjects, the curriculum includes Creative Writing, Personal Finance, STEM, and Computer Lab work. children.text: Middle School (Grades 6–8): The curriculum deepens students’ subject knowledge and continues to develop their critical thinking and independent learning habits. It includes core subjects, specialist instruction, electives, and enrichment activities. Project-based learning, digital tools, and SEL are embedded throughout.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi middle school student writing in class

children.text: In middle school, assessment includes a range of formative and summative methods to monitor progress and measure achievement. Formative assessments, such as quizzes, classwork, homework, projects, presentations, discussions, and teacher observations, are used throughout the learning process to provide feedback and support improvement. Summative assessments, including unit tests, end-of-term examinations, major projects, and performance tasks, evaluate student learning at the end of a unit or term.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi middle school teacher guiding students at their desks in class

children.text: Students are assessed across core subjects such as English, Mathematics, Science, Arabic, Islamic Studies, and UAE Social Studies, as well as additional subjects including Physical Education, Music, ICT/Technology, and other electives. Assessment methods may include written tests, research projects, essays, presentations, laboratory investigations, group work, and digital portfolios, with a focus on standards-based learning and mastery of key skills and knowledge.

children.text: Under the policy of using the Arabic language in education and in line with the directives of ADEK and the UAE Ministry of Education, Sharjah American International School has developed a structured plan for teaching Arabic Language, Islamic Education, and Social Studies at the Kindergarten stage. This policy aims to strengthen early language, social, and religious skills through age-appropriate learning experiences, promote national identity and a sense of belonging, ensure equal access to learning the official language of the country, and support cultural understanding and inclusion within the diverse community of the UAE.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi kindergarten student smiling at her desk

cards.description:
The Cognitive Abilities Test (CAT4) helps us understand how students learn and their academic potential. Students in Grades 3–9 take this assessment upon enrollment to identify their learning styles, enabling teachers to:

•	Adapt teaching approaches and materials
•	Adjust instructional pace and emphasis
•	Implement differentiated instruction

CAT4 measures four types of reasoning:

•	Verbal Reasoning - Understanding and reasoning through words
•	Quantitative Reasoning - Using numerical skills for problem-solving
•	Non-verbal Reasoning - Problem-solving using visual information
•	Spatial Ability - Thinking and drawing conclusions in three dimensions

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi students working on a written task in class

cards.title: CAT4 Assessment

cards.description:
Students in Grades 3–9 participate in MAP testing three times throughout the academic year. These computer-adaptive assessments:

•	Produce accurate data about each student’s learning level
•	Identify areas of strength and opportunity
•	Measure overall performance in core subjects
cards.title: NWEA MAP Testing

cards.description: To benchmark Arabic language proficiency against international standards, our students participate in IBT Arabic examinations conducted by ACER. This assessment provides valuable comparative data on student performance relative to peers in the region and worldwide.
cards.title: IBT Arabic Testing

cards.description:
The New Group Reading Test (NGRT) measures reading skills against national averages. This standardized assessment evaluates:

•	Phonics knowledge
•	Reading comprehension
•	Decoding ability
•	Vocabulary development
•	Grammatical understanding
•	Deduction and inference skills
•	Understanding of figurative and idiomatic language
cards.title: NGRT Testing

children.text: We are fully committed to ensuring that every student receives the support, opportunities, and encouragement needed to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. We believe that every learner is unique and deserves access to a high-quality education that recognizes and nurtures their individual strengths and needs.

The Inclusion Department works collaboratively with students, families, teachers, and external specialists to provide personalized support and targeted interventions. Through evidence-based practices, individualized planning, classroom accommodations, and continuous progress monitoring, we strive to remove barriers to learning and promote student success.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi kindergarten students learning together in class

children.text: Our services support students with Additional Learning Needs (ALN), gifted and talented learners, English Language Learners (ELL), students requiring Arabic Language Support, and those who may benefit from social, emotional, or behavioral support. Arabic Language Support is provided through targeted interventions designed to strengthen students’ Arabic language proficiency, enhance their access to the curriculum, and build confidence in their communication skills.
Guided by the values of respect, equity, and excellence, we aim to create a learning environment where all students feel valued, empowered, and equipped to reach their full potential.
